q: Which US consensus standard for occupational health and safety management systems, first released in 2005, includes requirements to identify and control hazards at the design and redesign stages and through management of change?
explain: Lyon identifies ANSI Z10, originally released in 2005 and updated in 2012, as one of the first US standards to include requirements for design safety reviews, risk assessment, procurement, and management of change within an OHS management system.

q: Why are guards for grinding wheels made of heavier material than most other machine guards?
options: To act as a heat sink for the wheel
To contain fragments if the wheel fractures and flies apart
To dampen noise from the grinding operation
To support the workpiece during grinding
explain: Grinding wheel guards both keep operators from contacting the wheel and contain fragments if the wheel fractures and flies apart. As a result, they are made of much heavier material and keep the operating opening to a minimum.

q: Part of a manufacturing building will store nitrocellulose-based materials that are likely to burn with extreme rapidity or produce explosions. How should the hazard of contents for this area be classified?
explain: NFPA 101 classifies contents that are likely to burn with extreme rapidity or from which explosions are likely as high hazard. Life safety requirements are more restrictive for high-hazard contents.

q: A site tracks near misses. Which version of the near-miss metric serves best as a leading indicator of the robustness of the safety process?
options: Total count of near misses reported each month
Ratio of near misses to recordable injuries each year
Number of near misses classified as high severity
Percentage of employees who participate in near-miss reporting
explain: Yates, citing La Duke, notes that near misses themselves are past events; it is participation in near-miss reporting, not the number of near misses, that serves as a good leading indicator because reporters are more engaged and better at identifying hazards.

q: A crane incident involved a signal person, crane operator, rigger, and a changing wind condition over a 4-minute period. The investigator wants a chart showing each actor's actions along a timeline with conditions inserted in logical order. Which method fits best?
explain: The multilinear events sequencing (MES) method uses a timeline chart in which every event is a single action by a single actor, with conditions inserted in the time flow; countermeasures are developed by examining each event.

q: A PHA of a cold-storage facility evaluated low temperature and hand-tool vibration as separate hazards, each with acceptable risk. What limitation of PHA should concern the reviewer?
options: PHA cannot be used during the design phase
PHA reviews hazards singly and can miss combined effects
PHA cannot identify the system energy sources
explain: Popov et al., citing Clemens, note that PHA does not readily recognize calamities from coexisting faults, and because hazards are analyzed individually, synergistic effects such as cold plus vibration can be missed.

q: A robber has just left a store. What should employees do first?
options: Clean the counter so the store can reopen quickly
Let witnesses leave and gather their contact details later
Lock the doors and call the police
Review the camera footage with customers present
explain: Friend and Kohn state that after the robber leaves, employees should immediately lock the doors and call police, ask witnesses to stay and not discuss the incident, and avoid touching surfaces the perpetrator may have touched.

q: A manufacturer adopts a fair-wage policy, improves working conditions, and sponsors local youth sports. Which triple bottom line dimension do these actions primarily address?
explain: Yates describes the people dimension as treating employees as part of the wider community: paying fair wages, ensuring humane working conditions, and supporting local communities.

q: A machine guard uses a spring with a constant of 2,000 N/m compressed 0.3 m. Using PE = ½kx², how much energy is stored that could be released during maintenance?
explain: Elastic potential energy is ½kx²: PE = 0.5 × 2,000 × (0.3)² = 0.5 × 2,000 × 0.09 = 90 J. Stored mechanical energy must be released or blocked during maintenance.

q: A trainer prepares a hazard communication session for workers with low literacy. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Assign the full written program to be read as homework
Use pictograms, demonstrations, and practice; read instructions aloud
Call on each worker in turn to read a section aloud
Use a timed written exam as the main learning activity
explain: OSHA's training resource recommends methods requiring little or no reading, reading instructions aloud, never calling on someone who does not volunteer, and using photos, pictograms, demonstrations, and hands-on practice.
